items.title: AI virtual cell technology could reveal how genetic changes and drugs alter cells
items.excerpt: Texas A&M's PertReason model predicts how genetic perturbations and drugs alter cell behavior and traces the biological pathways behind the change; its PertReasonQA benchmark checks whether LLMs reach right answers with the right evidence (arXiv, NeurIPS 2026).

history_match.title: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease

items.title: Optimized supercomputer workflow accelerates protein-structure prediction
items.excerpt: An LLNL-led team harnessed the El Capitan exascale supercomputer to massively accelerate AI protein-structure prediction, cutting the compute time needed to generate predicted structures for drug discovery and biology.

history_match.title: Less data, faster discovery: Researchers rethink AI's role in developing new materials

items.title: New AI tool exposes plant pathogens and the genes behind them
items.excerpt: Leiden University bioinformatician Guillermo Guerrero Egido's machine-learning tool bacLIFE compares the genomes of more than 16,000 plant-associated bacteria at once. It predicts each one's lifestyle (soil, plant-beneficial or pathogenic) and flags the genes likely behind disease-causing ability, which could help spot new crop pathogens and useful farm microbes earlier.

history_match.title: Rice plants can fight off devastating disease after gene editing with AI-designed tool

items.title: Scientists Use AI-Designed CRISPR to Make Disease-Resistant Rice
items.excerpt: University of Missouri's Bing Yang adapted Profluent's AI-designed OpenCRISPR-1 editor for plants, knocking out three SWEET genes in rice with up to 97% efficiency; edited plants resisted three bacterial blight strains and passed edits to offspring.

history_match.title: Rice plants can fight off devastating disease after gene editing with AI-designed tool

items.title: Catching AI's Mistakes Is a Mental Burden—and a Drag on Productivity
items.excerpt: A cognitive engineer explains the 'verification burden': productivity gains from AI are offset by the time and mental effort spent checking output, an instance of Woods' responsibility-authority double bind.

items.title: Supervised deep learning for efficient cryo-EM image alignment in drug discovery with cryoPARES
items.excerpt: cryoPARES is a deep-learning pose-estimation method trained on pre-aligned cryo-EM datasets that aligns particles far faster than traditional approaches and prunes particles automatically, removing manual steps from high-throughput structure determination.

items.title: Machine-learning-driven identification of cooperative descriptors for polysulfide conversion on spinel oxides
items.excerpt: A machine-learning-assisted approach uncovers two cooperative structural descriptors governing polysulfide conversion across spinel oxides and uses them to screen for high-performance lithium-sulfur battery catalysts.

items.title: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
items.excerpt: Researchers built a DNA-based molecular neural network whose neurons carry pH-tunable activation thresholds, letting the network rewire its connectivity in response to its chemical environment without changing composition.

history_match.title: Quantum neural networks with high-dimensional quantum neurons

items.title: Your Best Quantum Error Correction Engineer Might Be a Bot
items.excerpt: An analysis of how AI is taking an increasingly central role in designing new quantum error-correcting codes and decoders, from neural decoders to AI-searched code constructions.

history_match.title: Yonsei University Researchers Develop Mamba State-Space Neural Decoder to Enable Real-Time Quantum Error Correction

items.title: How AI can identify the magnetic structures behind high-frequency energy loss
items.excerpt: Tokyo University of Science used interpretable AI (persistent homology plus energy-landscape mapping) on micromagnetic simulations of an iron-based nanocrystalline soft magnet, pinpointing domain-wall features that raise the energy barrier as frequency climbs (NPG Asia Materials).

items.title: Noninvasive brain interface uses AI suggestions to convey messages nearly three times faster
items.excerpt: Rutgers researchers paired a noninvasive BCI with a locally run fine-tuned language model that suggests words and phrases; healthy participants spelled meaning-based messages nearly three times faster than with dictionary prediction (IEEE TBME).

items.title: AI can identify themes in human interviews but still misses nuances in meaning
items.excerpt: University of Missouri's AURA framework compared BERTopic topics with human-coded themes from 32 interviews (International Journal of Qualitative Methods): 11 of 12 human themes matched an AI topic, but the model merged or split themes and missed contextual meaning.

items.title: Sand grain-sized wireless chip can monitor reactions to provide data for self-driving labs
items.excerpt: A sand-grain-sized wireless sensor chip checks reaction temperature in real time, producing thousands of data points per hour to train the AI models that steer self-driving labs.

items.title: The AI Riemann hypothesis proof is almost certainly true, independent mathematicians attest
items.excerpt: Independent mathematicians say they are near to completing verification of the claimed AI-assisted solution to the Riemann hypothesis and that it is almost certainly correct. Follow-up to the same-day announcement; curator should pick one Riemann item.

history_match.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to prove Riemann hypothesis, most famous problem in all of math

items.title: AI helps researchers investigate how thousands of medical studies share code
items.excerpt: Researchers used AI to examine nearly 4,000 studies and hundreds of code repositories, finding gaps in the information needed to scrutinize and reuse published prediction research.

items.title: The Communal Brain Behind RFD4-Proteina
items.excerpt: IPD describes RFD4-Proteina, a generative protein-design model co-developed with NVIDIA that merges the RFdiffusion and Proteina-Complexa lineages and delivers 5-10x the throughput of high-quality designs. Same story as the R&D World enzyme item.

history_match.title: Nvidia, UW Institute for Protein Design unveil open-source protein design AI model

items.title: How NVIDIA and David Baker's lab designed an enzyme with AI
items.excerpt: Off-list (on-list IPD post lacks results): RFD4-Proteina designed metal-binding enzymes that break down the pesticide paraoxon; 89 of 288 designs were active vs 0 of 192 RFD3 designs, and six had 10-1,000x higher catalytic efficiency than earlier designs. Paper at rfd4-proteina.org, code on RosettaCommons.

history_match.title: Nvidia, UW Institute for Protein Design unveil open-source protein design AI model

items.title: NVIDIA Introduces Nemotron for Science to Accelerate Discoveries With Agents
items.excerpt: Off-list (scientific foundation model release, no on-list coverage found): NVIDIA launched Nemotron for Science at SC26, open science-tuned models, an open chemistry dataset and post-training tools for agentic scientific discovery.

items.title: Using AI to accelerate neuroscience research
items.excerpt: Neuroscience 2026 roundup (Tsinghua, UC Irvine, Berkeley Lab): a learning principle shared by artificial neural networks and fruit flies, a plain-English genomic-analysis tool, and brain-data standards. Conference presentations, no journal paper.

items.title: 'The first species we might be able to communicate with... might be a bird': An animal researcher explains how she decoded birdsong
items.excerpt: UC Berkeley computational neuroethologist Julie Elie explains how machine learning combined with behavioral experiments decoded specific zebra finch calls, and why birds may be the first species humans converse with.

items.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
items.excerpt: York University's Kohitij Kar tested brain-predicting vision ANNs in the reverse direction and found that even models that closely predict primate visual-cortex activity can rely on internal processes the brain does not use, questioning their reliability as neuroscience models.

history_match.title: This AI finds patterns in visual brain activity and turns them into pictures

items.title: University of California, San Diego, QuEra, and Collaborators Introduce Multi-Agent LLM Compiler Qubrio for Neutral-Atom Processors
items.excerpt: UC San Diego, Rice, QuEra, RIT and UW-Madison built Qubrio, a multi-agent LLM compiler that automates qubit placement, AOD routing and scheduling for neutral-atom processors; versus PowerMove on circuits up to 78 qubits it cut runtime 4.7x and raised fidelity 1.3x on average (arXiv 2611.02269).

items.title: Claude, find me a planet: amateur astronomers are using AI with mixed results
items.excerpt: Amateur Pavel Rabtsevich had Claude Code sift TESS data on 120,000+ stars; it flagged two likely planets around TIC 4206066 (3- and 11-day dips) that TESS astronomers have now added to the official candidate list, while experts like UBC's Michelle Kunimoto warn many AI-found claims are not validated. Off-list exception: no on-list outlet covered it.

items.title: Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
items.excerpt: University of Luxembourg (Alexandre Tkatchenko) built the QVib benchmark (293 molecules, 1,366 conformers, peptides and p53 assemblies) and showed machine-learned force fields reproduce DFT-level vibrations and experimental infrared spectra of proteins far better than classical force fields, with SO3LR giving the best accuracy-cost balance. Off-list exception.

items.title: Dueling claims of Riemann hypothesis proofs emerge
items.excerpt: Hours after Anthropic's Levent Alpöge posted a Claude-generated proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a second, competing claimed proof emerged. Formal-math follow-up (deprioritized; Riemann already covered 11-21).
